This applies to all family members, including children, who will be automatically registered when one parent registers. The registration can be done online or in person at a Bürgerbüro (citizen's office), and only one parent or an authorized person needs to appear in person. You need to bring valid identification for all persons to be registered and a confirmation from your landlord about your move-in date and address. Registration is free of charge, except if you want to update your vehicle registration, which costs a small fee [S1][S2][S3][S4].

Your next steps:
- Prepare valid ID documents for all family members.
- Obtain a landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) with all required details.
- Register online or visit a Bürgerbüro in Munich within two weeks of your move-in date.
- If you have a vehicle, bring the vehicle registration documents if you want to update your address there.
- If you cannot attend personally, authorize someone with a power of attorney to register on your behalf.

To register your address (Anmeldung) in Berlin, you need the following documents:

1. Identification proof:
   - For online registration: A valid ID card or EU citizen card (eID card) with activated online ID function (eID) and your PIN.
   - For in-person registration: A valid ID card or passport for German nationals; for foreigners, a national passport or passport substitute, possibly together with your electronic residence permit (eAT). Bring original documents for all persons moving in.

2. Confirmation of residence from your landlord (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung):
   - This must be provided by your landlord within two weeks after your move-in, including landlord's name and address, owner's name if different, move-in date, apartment address, and names of persons registering.
   - A rental contract alone is not sufficient.

3. If applicable:
   - Consent declaration from the other parent if registering a minor child and only one parent is present.
   - Birth, marriage, or other civil status certificates if this is your first registration in Berlin.
   - Power of attorney if someone else registers on your behalf.

These documents are required whether you register online or in person at the Bürgeramt (citizen office) [S2][S4].

- You need to have clarified your identity and nationality.

- You must hold a permanent residence permit, a Blue Card EU, or a residence permit that leads to permanent residence.
- You must be able to support yourself and your dependents without relying on social welfare benefits.
- You must have sufficient German language skills (at least B1 level).
- You must have knowledge of the legal and social order and living conditions in Germany, usually proven by passing a naturalization test.
- You must not have been convicted of a criminal offense.

Your next steps:
- Check that you meet the five-year residence requirement.
- Gather documents proving your identity, residence status, and language skills.
- Prepare for and pass the naturalization test.

The previous requirement to renounce your former nationality has been abolished, so you can hold both German and Indian citizenship simultaneously if allowed by Indian law [S7].

Congratulations on your marriage! 

As a married couple in Germany, you are initially assigned tax class (Steuerklasse) 4 for both spouses automatically at the time of your marriage [S3]. This is the standard tax class for married couples who live together and are both subject to unlimited income tax liability.

You have the option to change your tax class combination by application. The common choices are:

- Tax class 4/4: Both spouses have roughly equal incomes and are taxed similarly.
- Tax class 3/5: One spouse has a significantly higher income and chooses tax class 3 (lower tax burden), while the other spouse with the lower income chooses tax class 5 (higher tax burden). This combination can result in a higher net monthly income for the household but may lead to a tax adjustment when filing the annual income tax return [S1, S5].

There is also a third option called the factor method (Faktorverfahren) with tax class 4/4 with a factor, which aims to avoid large tax refunds or payments at the end of the year by calculating a factor that adjusts the withholding tax more precisely according to your combined income [S3, S4].

Should you pick tax class 3/5? It depends on your income difference:
- If one spouse earns significantly more than the other, 3/5 can be beneficial for monthly cash flow.
- If your incomes are similar, 4/4 or 4/4 with factor is usually better to avoid surprises at tax return time.

Your next steps:
- Decide if your incomes are very different or similar.
- If different, consider applying for tax class 3/5.
- If similar, consider staying with 4/4 or applying for 4/4 with factor.
- Submit the application for tax class change to your local tax office (Finanzamt) using the official form "Antrag auf Lohnsteuer-Ermäßigung und zu den Lohnsteuerabzugsmerkmalen" with the annex "Steuerklassenwechsel" [S3].
- Remember that choosing 4/4 with factor requires you to file an income tax return annually [S3].

If you want, I can help you with more details or the application process. Just let me know!
